name: DataTable
statusNote: DataTable ships on GitHub settings and security pages, but its scope is deliberately small: columns, sorting, row groups, densities, a skeleton and a separate pagination footer. It has no row selection, sticky header, column resizing or virtualisation, and its responsive column widths are still a TODO.
summary: A grid table of rows built from a column definition list: per-column width rules, start or end alignment, row headers, client-side or external sorting, optional row groups, three cell densities, a loading skeleton, and a container with title, subtitle, actions and a pagination footer. Choose it for tabular records the user scans and sorts; choose an ActionList or a plain list for single-column items.

inputs.name: columns
inputs.description: Column definitions: header (text or render function), field (dot path into the row) or id, renderCell, align (start or end), rowHeader, sortBy (true, 'alphanumeric', 'basic', 'datetime' or a comparator), width ('grow' default, 'growCollapse', 'auto' or an explicit length), minWidth, maxWidth.

inputs.name: data
inputs.description: Rows (each with a unique id, or use getRowId), row groups ({groupId, label, rows, aria-label}), or a mix in display order.

inputs.name: initialSortColumn
inputs.description: Column id or field the data arrives sorted by; the column must be sortable.

inputs.name: initialSortDirection
inputs.description: Direction of the initial sort; without initialSortColumn it applies to the first sortable column.

inputs.name: externalSorting
inputs.description: Do not reorder rows; only track and show the sort state and report clicks, for server-side sorting.

inputs.name: onToggleSort
inputs.description: Called with the column id and the new direction (ASC or DESC) on every sortable header click.

inputs.name: getRowId
inputs.description: Returns a row's unique id; defaults to row.id.

inputs.name: ariaLabelledBy
inputs.description: Id of the Table.Title that names the table (and its scroll region).

inputs.name: ariaDescribedBy
inputs.description: Id of the Table.Subtitle that describes the table.

inputs.name: title
inputs.description: Table.Title in Table.Container: the table's heading (h2 by default) with an id.

inputs.name: subtitle
inputs.description: Table.Subtitle in Table.Container, with an id.

inputs.name: actions
inputs.description: Table.Actions in Table.Container: buttons at the end of the title row.

inputs.name: divider
inputs.description: Table.Divider in Table.Container: a rule under the title row.

inputs.name: pagination
inputs.description: Table.Pagination in Table.Container: aria-label (required), totalCount (required), pageSize (default 25), defaultPageIndex, showPages (boolean or per range; default hides page numbers at narrow widths), onChange({pageIndex}). It does not slice data; the caller does.

inputs.name: skeletonRows
inputs.description: Table.Skeleton rows: placeholder lines per column while loading; Table.Skeleton takes the same columns and cellPadding.

anatomy.name: Container
anatomy.description: A two-column grid (title | actions, then full-width divider, subtitle, filter, table and footer rows) with 8px between the columns.

anatomy.name: Title
anatomy.description: Body-medium semibold text in --fgColor-default on a 20px line, centred against the actions.

anatomy.name: Actions
anatomy.description: A row of controls 8px apart, end-aligned in the title row.

anatomy.name: Scroll region
anatomy.description: A box around the table that scrolls it horizontally (and vertically if constrained) when it overflows.

anatomy.name: Table
anatomy.description: A grid whose columns come from the column definitions, 12px text on 20px lines, on --bgColor-default.

anatomy.name: Header cell
anatomy.description: Semibold --fgColor-muted text on --bgColor-muted, with a top border; --fgColor-default when the column is sorted.

anatomy.name: Sort button
anatomy.description: An unstyled button filling a sortable header's content: the header text, then the sort icon 8px after it (before it for end-aligned columns).

anatomy.name: Cell
anatomy.description: A flex box, content centred vertically, padded by density, 1px --borderColor-default bottom border; the row's first and last cells carry the table's side borders.

anatomy.name: Row header cell
anatomy.description: A cell in a rowHeader column: semibold --fgColor-default.

anatomy.name: Group header
anatomy.description: A full-width row before a group's rows: label (semibold --fgColor-default) then row count (--fgColor-muted), 8px apart, on --bgColor-muted with side and bottom borders.

anatomy.name: Skeleton
anatomy.description: Loading state: the real header row, then one row whose cells each stack skeletonRows shimmering text bars separated by row borders.

anatomy.name: Pagination
anatomy.description: A footer bar continuing the table's border (no top border, rounded bottom corners): the range text at the start, Previous, page numbers and Next at the end.

variants.description: Cell content and header text start-aligned.
Cell content end-aligned; a sortable header puts its icon before its text.

layout.text: Each column becomes one grid track: grow (the default) is minmax(max-content, 1fr), sharing free width but never narrower than its widest cell; grow with a maxWidth is minmax(auto, maxWidth); growCollapse is minmax(0, 1fr), shrinking below its content; auto is sized to its widest cell and never takes free width; an explicit width (number = px) is exactly that. A minWidth or maxWidth replaces the computed lower or upper bound.

The table is a grid on --bgColor-default at 12px text with 20px lines; head, body, group and row boxes adopt the table's column tracks (subgrid, or pass-through where subgrid is unsupported), so every cell in a column shares one width.

Cells are padded block/inline 4/8px (condensed), 8/12px (normal) or 12/16px (spacious); the first cell of every row pads 16px at its start and the last cell 16px at its end in every density, so text aligns with the container edge.
Cells are flex boxes with content centred vertically; an end-aligned cell or header justifies its content to the end.

Borders are drawn per cell, each --borderWidth-thin --borderColor-default: every header and body cell has a bottom border, header cells a top border, the first cell of each row a start border and the last cell an end border; there is no outer frame.

The header row's outer top corners round at 6px; the last body row's outer bottom corners round at 6px only when the scroll region is the last child of its parent, so a pagination footer below squares them off and draws its own rounded bottom.
A sortable header's button holds the text and the sort icon 8px apart; in an end-aligned column the icon comes first.
A group header spans all columns, padded like a cell, with label and count on a shared baseline 8px apart, its own side and bottom borders, on --bgColor-muted.

The container is a grid of two equal columns: title and actions share row 1, then divider, subtitle, filter, table and footer each span both columns, with 8px between columns. The title is body-medium semibold on a 20px line; the divider is 1px with 16px above and 8px below; a table directly after the title, subtitle or actions gets 8px above it.

The skeleton keeps the real header row and column tracks; each body cell drops its padding and stacks skeletonRows items, each padded like a cell and separated by bottom borders, holding a text bar whose width cycles 85, 67.5, 80, 60 and 75% of the cell.
Each skeleton bar is a SkeletonText line: --text-body-size-medium tall, --borderRadius-small corners, --skeletonLoader-bgColor, with half the leading of --text-body-lineHeight-medium above and below.

The pagination bar spans the container's footer row: 8px block and 16px inline padding, the range text at the start and the steps at the end (space-between, 16px apart at least), a --borderWidth-thin --borderColor-default border without a top edge, and --borderRadius-medium bottom corners.

The range reads 'start‒end of total' in --text-body-size-small --fgColor-muted. Previous and Next are body-medium buttons with 8px padding and --borderRadius-medium, 16px from the page numbers, in --fgColor-accent with a chevron when available and --fgColor-muted without one when not. Page buttons are at least 32px square with 8px block and 6px inline padding and --borderRadius-medium; a truncation step is a 32px square ellipsis.

Page numbers show the first and last page, two pages either side of the current one and ellipses for the gaps; with showPages false for a range (by default narrow, below 768px) only Previous and Next show and their 16px margins collapse. Regular is from 768px, wide from 1400px.

states.text: Hovering a row fills its cells (not skeleton cells) with --control-transparent-bgColor-hover; rows are not otherwise interactive.
Hovering an unsorted sortable header (or focusing its button) reveals the ascending icon as a preview; at rest an unsorted header shows no icon.
The sorted column's header text turns --fgColor-default and shows the ascending or descending icon permanently.
The skeleton bars shimmer: a 75-degree mask sweeps across over --base-duration-1000, repeating, only when the user has not asked for reduced motion.
Hovering or focusing an available Previous or Next or any page number fills it with --control-transparent-bgColor-hover.
The current page is --fgColor-onEmphasis on --bgColor-accent-emphasis; with keyboard focus it adds a 2px --bgColor-accent-emphasis outline inset 2px and a 3px inset --fgColor-onEmphasis ring.
Previous on the first page and Next on the last are aria-disabled: muted, no chevron, no hover fill, and activation does nothing, but they stay focusable.

behaviour.text: Activating a sortable header sorts by it ascending; activating the sorted header again flips between descending and ascending. There is no unsorted step after the first sort, and only one column sorts at a time.

Client-side sorting sorts a copy of the rows: true and 'basic' compare with < and ===, 'alphanumeric' compares digit runs numerically and other runs with localeCompare, 'datetime' compares Dates or timestamps, a function is a custom comparator on whole rows. Blank values (null, undefined, empty string) sort last in both directions, except with a custom comparator.
Row groups keep their positions while sorting; rows sort within each group and within each run of ungrouped rows.
With externalSorting the rows keep the caller's order; the header still shows the sort state and onToggleSort reports each click, so the caller re-fetches.
New data is re-sorted by the current sort; new columns drop the sort if its column is gone.
There is no empty state: with no rows the table renders its header row over an empty body, and the caller shows a Blankslate or message.

Pagination is separate from the table: it tracks pageIndex (from defaultPageIndex, else 0), pageSize (default 25) and totalCount, and calls onChange({pageIndex}) on every page change; the caller slices the rows shown. The range announces 'Showing start through end of total' through a status live region on change.

accessibility.role: table (with rowgroup, row, columnheader, rowheader and cell set explicitly); the overflowing scroll box is region; pagination is navigation
keyboard: Tab reaches each sortable header's button, then the scroll region if the table overflows, then the pagination buttons.
Enter or Space on a sortable header toggles its sort.
Enter or Space on Previous, Next or a page number changes page.
semantics: The table is named by aria-labelledby (the title) and described by aria-describedby (the subtitle); the scroll region reuses the label when it becomes a focusable region.
A sorted header carries aria-sort ascending or descending; its button's description is 'Sort ascending' or 'Sort descending' for the next action.
Row headers are th scope=row; in a table with groups every cell lists its column header, row headers and group header in headers.
A group header is a colgroup columnheader reading 'label, N rows'.
The current page has aria-current; page buttons read 'Page N'; Previous and Next read 'Previous page' and 'Next page'.

notes.text: There is no sticky header: the header row scrolls away with the body, and the scroll region scrolls the whole table. A native build that wants a pinned header adds it itself and must keep the header cells on the body's column tracks.
There is no row selection, row click or keyboard row navigation; rows are inert apart from the hover fill. Selection is built by the caller with a checkbox column via renderCell.
Pagination does not page the data; DataTable renders every row it is given, so the caller passes only the current page's slice.
The alphanumeric comparator returns -1, not 0, for two equal strings (it falls through to comparing group counts), so equal keys are not treated as ties; a port should return 0.
Skeleton bars use body-medium (14px) metrics while table text is 12px on 20px lines, so loading rows are slightly taller than loaded rows and the table jumps when data arrives.

The table's font size (0.75rem), line height (20/12), radius (0.375rem), cell paddings, title line height (20px), sort icon gap (0.5rem), page button minimum (2rem) and pagination gap (1rem) are literals, not tokens; the cell paddings live in component-local --cell-padding-block and --cell-padding-inline.
Pagination's ranges are literal px media queries (below 768px, from 768px, from 1400px), matching --breakpoint-medium and --breakpoint-xxlarge.

Sort buttons and Previous/Next carry no focus style in their modules (only the current page does); GitHub's global :focus-visible outline supplies one. A native build should draw the standard focus outline on them.
Under forced colours each skeleton bar gets a 1px transparent outline so it stays visible.

Column sizing is the CSS grid track algorithm over every cell (minmax with max-content, fr shares, subgrid rows); an immediate-mode build must measure every cell's content width in a first pass (or cache it per column), resolve tracks (fixed, then auto/max-content minimums, then share the remaining width by fr among grow and growCollapse columns, capped by maxWidth), then lay out rows. A table wider than its box scrolls rather than squeezing grow columns below their content.

Horizontal overflow is an overflow: auto box that becomes a focusable labelled region only once a ResizeObserver sees overflow; a native build clips the table, scrolls it horizontally, and makes the scroll box focusable (arrow keys scroll) when content exceeds it.

Header and cell text are not truncated; cells grow in height to fit wrapped content, and every cell in a row takes the row's tallest height (grid row sizing), which a native build must compute before painting row borders and the hover fill.
The shimmer is a CSS mask animation that respects prefers-reduced-motion; a native build animates a gradient over the bar and checks the platform's reduced-motion setting.
